主要内容: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has extended conditional exemptions from reporting and proxy delivery requirements for public companies, funds, and investment advisers affected by the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). This action was announced on March 25, 2020, as part of the SEC's ongoing efforts to monitor the impact of the virus on investors and capital markets. The extension provides public companies with a 45-day extension to file certain disclosure reports that would have been due between March 1 and July 1, 2020. The SEC also issued guidance on disclosure considerations related to COVID-19, encouraging companies to provide current and forward-looking information to investors while recognizing the challenges of assessing the virus's impact on businesses and markets. The order allows companies to rely on Form S-3 or Form F-3 eligibility if they were current as of the relief period's start and file any required reports within 45 days of the original deadline. Similarly, companies using Form S-8 or Rule 144(c) will be considered current if they meet these conditions. The SEC also encourages companies to disclose material information related to the Coronavirus and to avoid selective disclosures. Companies providing forward-looking information should consider the safe harbor provisions under Section 21E of the Exchange Act. Affected entities are advised to contact SEC staff for further assistance. The extension of the exemption period is from the date of the original order to August 15, 2020. The original order had extended the period to June 15, 2020. Entities seeking to rely on the exemption must notify the Division staff and/or investors of their intent to rely on the relief. The SEC has emphasized that the relief is temporary and subject to specific conditions. The orders are intended to provide flexibility while ensuring the protection of investors. The extension was initially set to expire on March 31, 2020, but has now been extended to June 30, 2020. The exemption allows for the delivery of required filings as soon as practicable, but no later than 45 days after the originally required date. The SEC has provided contact information for various forms and inquiries related to the impact of the Coronavirus on operations and compliance. This includes specific contact details for Form N-MFP, Form N-CR, Form N-LIQUID, Form ADV, and Form PF. The extension aims to provide relief to entities affected by the Coronavirus pandemic, ensuring they can meet regulatory requirements without undue hardship.
